name: Vercel Web Interface Guidelines
description: Deterministic checks for Vercel Web Interface Guidelines compliance: accessibility, focus management, forms, animation, typography craft, image discipline, performance, interaction safety, and anti-pattern detection. Bundled snapshot of vercel-labs/web-interface-guidelines fetched from https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vercel-labs/web-interface-guidelines/main/command.md

ruleExtensions.instruction: Every icon-only button must carry an aria-label, every form control must have a visible label or aria-label, interactive surfaces must use <button> or <a>/<Link> rather than <div onClick>, and images must declare alt or aria-hidden for decorative icons.

Interactive elements must expose a visible focus-visible indicator such as focus-visible:ring-* or an equivalent; outline:none is only allowed when paired with a focus-visible replacement, and sticky or overlay surfaces must never cover the focused element.
Motion must honor prefers-reduced-motion, animate only transform/opacity with explicitly listed properties (never transition: all), and interactive animations must remain interruptible mid-animation.
Every must declare explicit width and height to prevent layout shift, below-fold images must use loading="lazy", and critical above-fold images must use priority or fetchpriority="high".

Lists larger than fifty items must be virtualized or use content-visibility:auto, critical fonts must preload with font-display:swap, render must not read layout properties like getBoundingClientRect or offsetHeight, and text overflow must be handled with truncate, line-clamp, break-words, or min-w-0 on flex children.

Touch surfaces must declare touch-action:manipulation, modals and sheets must use overscroll-behavior:contain, destructive actions must require confirmation or undo, and any drag/swipe/pinch gesture must also have a tap/click and keyboard alternative.

Dates and numbers must format through Intl.DateTimeFormat and Intl.NumberFormat rather than hardcoded strings, and the UI must include an intentional empty state rather than rendering broken layouts for empty data.

tierB.name: vercelCraft
tierB.condition: only scored when the vercel-interface-guidelines extension is enabled
tierB.instruction: Score whether the interface follows Vercel-grade product discipline: crisp focus and hover states, correct a11y semantics, compositor-friendly motion with reduced-motion behavior, disciplined image and typography craft, and no flagged anti-patterns such as disabled zoom, unlabeled inputs, or transition: all.
